analyses.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
analyses.verdict: The highest-quality breakout in the market: a 52-week-high close on the lightest volume in its group, backed by 46.9% earnings growth at a 14.5x multiple.

financials.summary: JPMorgan's last full fiscal year was defined by the durability of net interest income long after the market expected it to compress, paired with a genuine recovery in the capital-markets businesses. The income statement carried strong NII alongside a rebound in investment banking fees and trading revenue as issuance and M&A pipelines reopened. The balance sheet remained the industry's fortress — CET1 comfortably above requirement with excess capital being returned through buybacks and a raised dividend — while credit costs normalized upward from unsustainably low levels rather than deteriorating. Cash generation supported both the buyback and continued technology investment. The scan's trailing figures show EPS up 46.9% and revenue up 30.4%, which is the quantitative signature of that operating leverage.
highlights: Trailing EPS growth +46.9% — the strongest of any large US bank in this scan
Trailing revenue growth +30.4%, driven by NII durability plus a capital-markets recovery
Forward P/E of 14.5x — a modest multiple for that growth rate
CET1 capital maintained well above regulatory minimums, funding buybacks and dividend growth
Credit costs normalizing from cycle lows rather than deteriorating

accomplishments: Held the #1 or #2 position across investment banking, markets, and US consumer deposits simultaneously
Converted the regional-bank dislocation of prior years into durable deposit and client share
Scaled AI deployment across fraud detection, client servicing and coding into measurable expense leverage
Sustained industry-leading return on tangible common equity through a full rate cycle

journey_52w.summary: A grinding, low-drama advance from a $280.14 low to a $362.02 close at the 52-week high — a 29% gain built without a single violent leg. The move accelerated in the last quarter as the market rotated out of AI-linked momentum and into cash-generative value, and the final approach to highs came on contracting volume, which is the mark of accumulation rather than chasing.

analyses.name: Marathon Petroleum Corporation
analyses.verdict: The purest expression of the Hormuz closure — 348% earnings growth at 11.3x forward, closing at a 52-week high with TradingView independently rating it Strong Buy.

financials.summary: Marathon's last full year was a refining-margin story from top to bottom. Crack spreads widened materially as global product supply tightened, and because refining is a spread business, that flowed to the bottom line with extreme operating leverage — the scan's trailing EPS growth of 348% against revenue growth of 53.7% is precisely that leverage, with earnings compounding far faster than the top line. The midstream segment through MPLX provided a stable, fee-based cash-flow floor underneath the volatile refining earnings, which is the structural reason Marathon can commit to buybacks through the cycle. Free cash flow was directed overwhelmingly at share repurchase, shrinking the count and amplifying per-share earnings further.
highlights: Trailing EPS growth +348% — the largest earnings inflection among energy large caps in this scan
Trailing revenue growth +53.7%, so the earnings gain is margin-driven, not just volume
Forward P/E of 11.3x despite the stock more than doubling off its $156.06 52-week low
MPLX midstream provides fee-based cash flow that is insulated from crack-spread volatility
Aggressive buyback program reducing share count and levering per-share earnings

accomplishments: Operated the largest US refining system at high utilization through a period of extreme margin volatility
Used peak-margin cash flow for buybacks rather than capacity expansion — the correct capital discipline at a cycle peak
Grew MPLX distributions, strengthening the non-refining cash-flow base
Captured widening product spreads created by global supply dislocation faster than peers

analyses.name: Valero Energy Corporation
analyses.verdict: The best-constructed chart among the refiners — 453% EPS growth with RSI only 59.4 at a 52-week high, and TradingView rates it Strong Buy.

financials.summary: Valero's last full fiscal year produced the most extreme earnings leverage in the scanned universe: trailing EPS growth of 453.5% on revenue growth of 51.7%. As the largest independent refiner with a Gulf Coast-weighted system, Valero captured widening light-heavy differentials and product cracks with minimal upstream exposure to dilute the spread. The renewable diesel and ethanol segments contributed a smaller but structurally growing earnings stream. The balance sheet carried low net leverage, and free cash flow went almost entirely to shareholders through buybacks and a well-covered dividend rather than into new capacity.

analyses.name: Arista Networks Inc.
analyses.verdict: The only AI-infrastructure name that closed at a 52-week high while the rest of the complex broke — full leadership confirmation with TradingView Strong Buy.

financials.summary: Arista's last full fiscal year was a demonstration that high-speed Ethernet is winning the AI back-end networking argument. Revenue growth of 37.7% with EPS growth of 35.7% shows the company scaled without sacrificing its unusually high gross margin — a rare combination in networking hardware, where volume usually comes at the cost of price. The software-driven EOS operating model keeps R&D leverage high and support revenue recurring. The balance sheet is debt-free with a large net cash position, and cash conversion remained strong even as inventory was built to serve hyperscaler lead times.

analyses.name: Dell Technologies Inc.
analyses.verdict: A genuine momentum reset — RSI back to 49.7 after an 84.7% three-month run — with TradingView's most lopsided confirmation in the scan at 15 buy / 1 sell.

financials.summary: Dell's last full fiscal year was dominated by the AI server ramp. Trailing revenue growth of 87.5% with EPS growth of 282.5% reflects the Infrastructure Solutions Group scaling dramatically as enterprises and neoclouds built out GPU capacity, while the Client Solutions PC business provided a stable, cash-generative base. The critical nuance is margin: AI server gross margins are structurally thinner than Dell's traditional storage and PC mix, so revenue growth outpacing margin expansion is expected and not a warning by itself. Free cash flow supported both debt reduction and a growing capital-return program. Backlog and order-book disclosures became the metric the market watches more closely than reported revenue.

analyses.name: Amazon.com Inc.
analyses.verdict: The highest-quality mega-cap entry on the board — 242% EPS growth at 26.4x forward, in a base rather than a chase, with only 2.4% three-month momentum.

financials.summary: Amazon's last full fiscal year was the year the margin story finally caught up to the revenue story. Trailing EPS growth of 242.3% against revenue growth of 19.6% is the clearest possible illustration: the top line grew respectably while earnings multiplied, driven by North America retail margin expansion, the continued mix shift toward high-margin advertising, and AWS reaccelerating. Cost-to-serve improvements from regionalized fulfillment continued to compound. The offsetting pressure was capital intensity — AI and data-center capex ran at unprecedented levels, consuming free cash flow that would otherwise have flowed through. That capex line is now the single number the market reacts to.

analyses.verdict: A trillion-dollar-scale business still growing revenue 47.7% — and the chart is 1.7% off its high with RSI at only 58.4, so you are not chasing it.

financials.summary: Lilly's last full fiscal year was driven overwhelmingly by the incretin franchise. That gap between revenue and earnings growth is a choice, not a problem: capacity has been the binding constraint on the franchise, and the capex is what relieves it. Cash generation funded the build-out while supporting the dividend.

analyses.verdict: The best fundamentals in the entire scan attached to a chart that has quietly lost leadership — hold it, but the technicals do not support adding ahead of earnings in 16 days.

financials.summary: Liquidia's last full fiscal year was its transition from development-stage to commercial-stage. Trailing revenue growth of 4,158% is the arithmetic of launching a product off a near-zero base — the percentage is spectacular precisely because the denominator was tiny, and it should be read as evidence that the launch happened, not as a sustainable growth rate. Yutrepia, the dry-powder inhaled treprostinil formulation for pulmonary arterial hypertension and PH-ILD, is the entire story. The company remains at a stage where cash burn, script uptake, payer coverage and gross-to-net dynamics matter more than any conventional income-statement metric. A forward P/E of 15.2x on a name at this stage should be treated with caution — forward estimates for a first-year launch carry very wide error bars.
